description: The northern anchor of the Bada Char Dham, dedicated to Lord Vishnu as Badrinarayan, situated between Nar and Narayana mountain ranges.
history: Established by Adi Shankaracharya in the 8th century after retrieving the black Saligram idol from the Alaknanda River at Narad Kund.

description: Natural thermal sulphur water reservoirs situated along the banks of the Alaknanda below the main Badrinath temple.
history: Known for constant 45°C medicinal hot springs where pilgrims take a purification dip before entering the sanctum.

description: The 'First Indian Village' located 3 km beyond Badrinath, inhabited by the indigenous Indo-Tibetan Bhotia community.
history: An ancient trade gateway connecting India and Tibet via the Mana Pass, noted for wool weaving and herbs.

description: A 122-meter cliff waterfall dropping from glacial heights, located 6 km ahead of Mana village.
history: Tradition holds that the pure droplets of the fall turn away from anyone who harbors unrighteous thoughts.

description: The eastern anchor of the Bada Char Dham, dedicated to Lord Jagannath alongside Balabhadra and Subhadra.
history: Constructed in the 12th century by King Anantavarman Chodaganga of the Eastern Ganga dynasty, world-famous for its annual Ratha Yatra.

description: A 13th-century UNESCO World Heritage monumental temple engineered in the shape of a colossal chariot with 24 carved wheels.
history: Built around 1250 CE by King Narasimhadeva I of the Eastern Ganga dynasty to honor Surya, the Sun God.

description: A pristine Blue Flag-certified golden sand beach on the Bay of Bengal coast near Puri.
history: Developed into an eco-certified beach destination equipped with bathing infrastructure and coastal lifeguards.

description: A heritage crafts village near Puri where every household practices traditional Pattachitra cloth painting and palm-leaf engraving.
history: The birthplace of legendary Odissi dance guru Kelucharan Mohapatra, keeping century-old Gotipua dance and folk arts alive.

description: Asia's largest brackish water lagoon, where the lake meets the Bay of Bengal, home to rare Irrawaddy dolphins and migratory birds.
history: Designated India's first Ramsar wetland of international importance in 1981.

description: The southern anchor of the Bada Char Dham, renowned for its 22 sacred theerthams (wells) and the world's longest pillared corridors.
history: Expanded across centuries by the Pandya and Jaffna kings, with the monumental 1,200-meter corridor built by the Setupati rulers of Ramanathapuram.

description: The sacred sea beach situated right in front of the eastern entrance of the Ramanathaswamy Temple.
history: Pilgrims take their first purificatory sea bath here before proceeding inside the temple to bathe in the 22 interior wells.

description: A historic coastal ghost town destroyed in the 1964 cyclone, marking where the Indian Ocean meets the Bay of Bengal.
history: An active port and railway link to Sri Lanka until December 22, 1964, when a severe cyclone submerged the entire town.

description: India's first cantilever sea bridge (opened 1914), connecting mainland India across the Palk Strait.
history: Engineered under British rule to connect mainland India (Mandapam) to Rameswaram Island across the Palk Strait.

description: A grand national memorial and museum constructed at the burial site of India's 11th President, Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam.
history: Inaugurated in 2017 by the DRDO, displaying Kalam's personal artifacts, missile replicas, and hand-painted murals.

description: The western anchor of the Bada Char Dham, dedicated to Lord Krishna as the King of Dwarka with a 52-yard flag atop its 5-story spire[cite: 1].
history: The current Jagat Mandir structure was built in the 16th century in Chalukya architecture over ancient sanctum foundations[cite: 1].

description: An island sanctuary situated in the Gulf of Kutch, revered as the residential palace of Lord Krishna.
history: Archaeological excavations reveal settlement layers dating back to the late Harappan era; connected via the cable-stayed Sudarshan Setu.

description: One of the 12 sacred Jyotirlinga shrines of Lord Shiva, featuring a 25-meter tall seated Shiva statue in Daarukavanam.
history: Mentioned in the Shiva Purana as Nageshvara Jyotirlinga, symbolizing protection from all poisons and earthly harms.

description: A 12th-century stone temple dedicated to Lord Krishna's chief queen Rukmini, adorned with rich carvings of elephants and musicians.
history: Built 2 km away from Dwarkadhish Temple due to the mythological curse of Sage Durvasa separating Krishna and Rukmini.

description: A Blue Flag-certified eco-beach near Dwarka with pristine waters and marine adventure sports infrastructure.
history: Developed into an international standard beach with clean waters and conservation measures for local marine life.
